scope: scripts/qualify_motion_connections.py on a frozen Debug build of 79245419 (artifacts/um5, git archive), 44/44 steps, in an owned scratch CPU 1511-1 PN V4.1 with a TM PosInput 2 V2.0 (channel 0 MotionControl), an AQ 2xU/I ST and a SINAMICS G120C PN on the CPU's IO system. Applied with checkpoint, PLC compile and save, read back through technology_read and equal after a fresh Portal reopen: a TO_ExternalEncoder 10.0 encoder on the TM PosInput item (Connect(DeviceItem)), replaced through Connect(DeviceItem, DeviceItem, ConnectOption.Default) and Connect(Int32 0, Int32 0, Default); a channel replacement restored from its checkpoint. Typed refusals UnsupportedTarget and InvalidRequest left the slots unchanged. V21 refusals recorded with exact errors and restored: TO_MeasuringInput on the TM PosInput item by channel index and on its channel (Target not available for input=0 and output=-1), TO_SpeedAxis actor on the AQ channel with Actor.Type 0 on a virtual axis (Target not available for input=-1 and output=-1), encoder on a PD_TEL83 DB member (No valid assignment for Encoder(MoEncoder)). The G120C exposes no telegram device item, so actor and torque on a telegram were not reached.
limitations: One owned scratch CPU 1511-1 PN V4.1; TO_PositioningAxis (virtual), TO_SpeedAxis (virtual, analog actor), TO_ExternalEncoder and TO_MeasuringInput 10.0. Only the encoder role connected; actor, torque and measuring input were refused by V21 or unreachable on this fixture.
The G120C PN added through Openness exposes no telegram device item even on the IO system (same root as the D10 DriveObjectNumber blocker), so drive telegram targets are not qualified.
Engineering only; nothing is downloaded and no axis moves; the drive is never compiled (no compiler service).
